summary: Tairyō Makita worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Shinryo Iwai and at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto Universities. He held posts at Kyoto University from 1949 to 1976 and served as president of Saitama Institute of Technology in 1997.
Taisen Deshimaru was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kodo Sawaki from around 1936 to 1965 and founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. His main academic career included serving as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1978 to 2005.
Taishun Mibu worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Taisho University from approximately 1934 to 1937 and later served there as library director from around 1953 to 1983.

Taitetsu Unno specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and earned an M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Tokyo, later serving at Smith College from 1971 to 1998.

Taitsu Kono focused on Buddhist studies. He studied at Hanazono University from 1950 to 1954, trained under Mumon Yamada from around 1954 to 1988, and later held a post at Hanazono University from around 1998 to 2004.

Taixu was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Jichan, Yang Wenhui, and Jing'an, and at Jinling Scriptural Press. He founded several institutes, including Wuchang Buddhist Institute, and led the Minnan Buddhist Institute in 1927.
Tak Pui Sze works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Sze pursued a PhD at the University of British Columbia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).

Taka Yanagisawa worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Japan Women's University, Yanagisawa served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties from around 1984 to 1989.

Takaaki Yoshimoto worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Yamagata University from around 1942 to 1945 and at Tokyo Institute of Technology from around 1945 to 1947, where he later held a post from roughly 1947 to 1950.

Takahiko Kameyama works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Attested in 2015, Kameyama held posts as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.
Takahiko Sato works in Buddhist studies. Sato held a post as a professor at Koyasan University, attested in 2015 and 2026.
Takahiro Kato works in Indology and philosophy. As attested for 2026, Kato serves as a professor at the University of Tokyo and holds a post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takaji Fukita specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University under Zenno Ishigami, at Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama, and under Heinz Bechert. He held a lectureship at Bukkyo University around 1996.
Takako Abe works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Abe held posts at Taisho University as a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026).

Takamaro Shigaraki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies. At Ryukoku University, he became professor in 1970 and served as president from 1989 to 1995.

Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. Yoshie taught at Waseda Junior and Senior High School and served at Waseda University as a lecturer and later as Dean of Letters in 1930.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Inoue studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and has served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takanobu Takahashi specialized in Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University. He served as associate professor of Indian literature at Shitennoji University and associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1999–2016).

Takanori Fukita works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Fukita studied as a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017), held a post at Bukkyo University, and was appointed special appointment faculty (lecturer) at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
